sentences.text: Dzungarisuchus is an extinct genus containing only one species of crocodile.
The only known remains consist of isolated postcranial bones and jaw fragments.
Fossils of this animal have been discovered in Xinjiang, China, dating to the late Eocene.
The genus was described by Dong in 1974.
All fossil material discovered so far belongs to the type species Dzungarisuchus manacensis.
Dzungarisuchus belongs to the subfamily Crocodylinae.
It is classified within the family Crocodylidae.
Dzungarisuchus lived during the Priabonian stage, between 37.71 and 33.9 million years ago.
